messages:
Alex: quick sync — after the RFC we discussed hybrid scoping (project-scoped API keys + org-admin tokens). want to align on migration approach and service auth for background jobs.
Mira: +1. my strong preference is to default to project-scoped keys for user-facing flows, and have a small set of org-level tokens only for infra/admin tasks. reduces blast radius.
Jeff: question — background workers sometimes need to touch multiple projects (billing, telemetry). do we expect them to hold org tokens or exchange into per-project ephemeral creds?
Mira: we shouldn't give long-lived org tokens to apps. recommend brokered short-lived tokens minted with limited audience and scope. token exchange flow: service -> broker -> ephemeral token (5m ttl) scoped to target project.
Sam: that aligns with what I sketched earlier. we can reuse operator-proxy for minting if we add a claim ("orig_service") and audience. exchange sample:```http
POST /token-exchange
{ "subject": "svc-a", "target_project": "proj-123", "scopes": ["read:billing"] }
```
Nina: ops/telemetry concern: we need to keep token attribution (who requested the mint) and have audit logs. any minted token must carry a stable request id and should be surfaced in traces.
Jeff: perf question — continuous exchange will add latency for high-throughput pipelines. can we allow broker to cache short-lived tokens per (svc,project,scope) tuple for 30s? cache would be TTL-limited and invalidated on policy change.
Mira: caching sounds fine if we gate it behind a policy. note: must still respect revocation. broker should check revocation cache on mint if cache hit is older than N seconds.
Alex: rollout plan idea: feature-flag the new path behind `authz_migration_mode`. start with read-only enforcement for 2 weeks, then enforced for 10% of traffic, then 100%. Nina will own telemetry dashboards.
Nina: I'll add dashboards for per-token usage, broker latencies, revocation hits/misses. also will add an alert if broker cache hit rate drops unexpectedly.
sec-bot: FYI — related RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2026-authn-hybrid-scoping (pinned).
Sam: one more: SDK ergonomics. client libs should expose `exchangeForProjectToken(targetProject, scopes)` so developers don't call broker API directly. fallback: if client cannot exchange, it should surface a clear error and suggest a retry/backoff.
Alex: decision checklist: 1) default project-scoped keys for user apps, 2) brokered short-lived tokens for cross-project service work, 3) cached ephemeral tokens allowed with strict TTL + revocation checks, 4) rollout via `authz_migration_mode` canary. any objections? :thumbsup: or say now.
Jeff: :thumbsup: from me.
Mira: :thumbsup: except we should add a migration task to rotate any existing long-lived org tokens within 90 days.
Nina: I'm OK, will coordinate telemetry and owner docs.
Alex: action items: @Mira create migration PR with token rotation plan, @Sam add SDK stub + error guidance, @Nina dashboard + alert, @Jeff help spec cache invalidation behaviour. I'll open the canary rollout ticket.
